title-xl.purpose: Section links in the side sheet (520); app step titles at the same step in 600.

lede.purpose: Sentence under the hero headline (max 34ch), line under an act title, app step text.

body.purpose: Running copy in slate soft, 62ch measure; panel text 30ch.

label.purpose: Step descriptions, demo status and cancel hint, the hero's stage line, button text.

shadows.purpose: Dark pill button and rail arrows (dropped when disabled).

shadows.name: sheet
shadows.purpose: Side sheet; thrown to the right, away from the edge it slides from.

shadows.name: ground-cast-hero
shadows.purpose: Ellipse under the hero chip; drawn as a background, not a box-shadow.

shadows.name: ground-cast
shadows.purpose: Ellipse under the app phone sketch; drawn as a background, not a box-shadow.

motion.name: sc-d-fast
motion.purpose: Button background, border and press transitions.

motion.name: sc-d-base
motion.purpose: Header bar turning white on scroll; back-to-top fade and 0.5rem slide-in.

motion.name: back-to-top
motion.value: visible after 1.2 viewports; smooth scroll to top, instant under prefers-reduced-motion (160ms opacity fade only); focus moves to the wordmark

motion.name: hold
motion.value: short press: group paths over 2.2s; hold 3s, then 5s cancel window (second press cancels), then the emergency path plays on its own over 5.2s; end state at once under reduced motion

motion.name: snowfall
motion.value: canvas particles, 22 on desktop, 12 below 700px; off under prefers-reduced-motion

motion.name: sc-d-slow
motion.purpose: Active-step underline growing across the step list.

motion.name: app-sketch
motion.value: route, track and radius drawn from the pinned act progress (--sc-p); end state under reduced motion

motion.name: hero-scrub
motion.value: 2.6 viewports, no dwell; footage scales 1 to 1.14 with --sc-p, headline block lifts 9vh (4vh on phones) and fades out by about 26%; the second line (h2) assembles line by line (kinetic lines) and holds from about 40% to 96%; chip and its cast rise 6vh and scale to 1.5; transforms off under reduced motion

motion.name: app-steps
motion.value: persistent list; active and passed headings turn ink over sc-d-slow, active bar ink; nothing fades out

motion.name: side-sheet
motion.value: slide in from translateX(-100%) over 260ms, out over 180ms, sc-ease-out; no animation under reduced motion; wordmark chevron rotates 180deg over sc-d-base while open

motion.name: doubt-lines
motion.value: driven by the act's --sc-p: each line slides in from -6vw and fades from 15% to full, staggered by 0.06 of progress; the closing word scales 0.82 to 1 and fades in from 50% progress; static under reduced motion

motion.name: photo-reveal
motion.value: the mountain photo frame wipes up (reveal up) as the act enters, with parallax inside the frame

motion.name: rail
motion.value: pinned act, 2.4 viewports; --sc-p drives scrollLeft, manual scroll, mouse drag and the arrows add a kept offset; snap off while driven; arrows step one panel width, smooth unless reduced motion; arrows disabled at the ends; not driven under reduced motion

narrative.overview:
The page is a bright winter morning. High-key snow white and pale glacier blue carry every surface; the only dark is slate ink, used for words, line drawings and the one action. The chip stands on that snow as a flat line drawing with a cold blue cast shadow underneath, the way a thing lies on fresh powder. Mountain footage (Mixkit stock) is scrubbed by scroll and dissolves downward into the white ground through a mask, never a drawn edge; a light snowfall on a canvas is the atmosphere of the first viewport.

Density is low and the air is generous. Each act of the scroll does one thing: a centred headline in the sky that gives way to a second line assembling itself, staggered lines of doubt sliding in from the left, the chip to try with a slope drawing that answers the press, a framed photo of a group on the mountain that wipes up into view, the app sketched in a phone outline, a sideways rail of typographic rider panels that vertical scroll carries along, then the team. The page is an introduction only: it ends with the team act and a plain footer, and has no rental or purchase surface. Honesty is a visual element: placeholders and sketches are labelled in a small caption directly under the thing they stand for, and the interactive demo carries a pill that says it is a demonstration.

The world refuses the dark gadget page with a glowing device and three feature cards. Colour is not decoration here: there is no accent hue at all, only ink-dark for action and a single emergency red that belongs to the alarm.

The scroll mechanism is the ScrollCraft engine (`scrollcraft.css`/`.js`, unchanged). This system is the set of overrides of its `--sc-*` tokens plus the page's own tokens and classes in `seite.css`; the engine's spacing and type scales are inherited as they are.
keyCharacteristics: High-key snow grounds, slate ink, no accent hue.
Emergency red appears only where the emergency itself is shown.
Flat slate line drawings (chip, slope, phone) with rounded caps; things that stand get a blurred cold blue cast ellipse.

Footage masked into the white ground and scrubbed: it zooms gently while the headline lifts and fades, the second line assembles line by line and the chip rises and grows to 1.5 with its cast; sparse snowfall as atmosphere, removed under reduced motion.
Soft, blue-tinted, offset shadows; hairlines in shadow blue, a 2px ink rule only for emphasis or the active step.
Every placeholder and sketch labelled where it stands.

rules.name: The No Accent Rule
rules.body: There is no brand hue. Action is slate ink on snow; nothing is turquoise, blue-filled or gradient-lit.

rules.name: The Red Is The Alarm Rule
rules.body: Emergency red marks the emergency and nothing else: not links, not errors, not prices, not decoration, not the group call, not a child leaving the radius. If a surface does not depict an emergency call, it has no red.

rules.name: The Mid-Weight Rule
rules.body: Display weights stay between 480 and 640; hierarchy comes from size and tracking, never from 800-weight shouting.

rules.name: The Sentence Headline Rule
rules.body: Headlines are short declarative German sentences with a full stop. Nothing sits above them; supporting lines go below.

rules.name: The Air Rule
rules.body: One idea per viewport. If an act needs a second idea, it gets its own scroll distance rather than a denser grid.

rules.name: The Cold Shadow Rule
rules.body: Shadows are blue, never black or grey, and they fall downward with blur (the side sheet's falls away from its edge). Hard offset shadows do not exist in this world.

rules.name: The Standing Object Rule
rules.body: A drawn thing that stands on the page gets a blurred cold blue ellipse beneath it, never a box shadow.

dos: Do keep every ground in the snow family (`snow-canvas`, `snow-surface`, `glacier-drift`) and let acts drift between them.
Do make the one action a slate ink pill; there is one per view. The back-to-top circle is fixed chrome, not a second action.
Do set a standing drawn object on a cold blue cast ellipse.
Do dissolve footage into the white ground with a mask, and label stock, sketches and placeholders honestly.
Do tint every shadow with the cold shadow hue and keep it blurred and offset downward.
Do keep snowfall sparse (22 flakes on desktop, 12 on phones); remove it, give drawn paths their end state and make scrolling instant under reduced motion.
Do draw people, group paths and objects in slate line work; ink is the emergency path and the active state.
donts: Don't introduce an accent hue; the engine accent stays slate ink.
Don't use emergency red for anything that is not the emergency itself.
Don't build a dark gadget page with a glowing device or a row of three feature cards; panels are typographic, without boxes.
Don't put kickers or eyebrows above headlines.
Don't use black or grey shadows, hard offset shadows, or drawn snowbanks; black exists only as a mask stop.
Don't show a placeholder object, sketch or team image without its caption.
